data_articles_fetched_then_excluded: themarker: "מהיכן תביא ישראל 65 מיליארד שקל כדי לשלם על F-35 ועל מטוסי התדלוק?" - paywalled beyond the lede paragraph; the retrieved text contained no verifiable figure matching the headline's '65 billion' claim, so it was dropped rather than audited on an incomplete body.
themarker: "לשתי הקבוצות העניות בישראל יש הזדמנות נדירה" - confirmed by fetch to be an opinion/commentary piece with no specific citable empirical claim, only political framing.

stories_list.note: CBS's own September 2026 wage release could not be read directly (site returned title-only pages / 404 on the guessed release URL); all 6 claims corroborated identically across 3 independent secondary outlets (Globes, Bizportal, Maariv), with one unverified sub-claim (the +0.3% YoY jobs figure, which conflicts with Globes' own +1.3%).

Haaretz is the sole outlet reporting the Meron committee legal-fee figures (NIS 570k/670k, ~3x the AG counsel's 200k recommendation); no independent corroboration or public document found in HE/EN search. Figures are internally consistent and not contradicted by anything found.

9/13 claims (Highway 20 speeds, CBS annual mileage stats, metro sites) corroborated by independent outlets (Globes, Bizportal, Maariv). 4/13 claims (Highway 1/40/44 figures from Netivei Israel, southbound Hwy 20 post-holiday speed) appear only in Globes in near-identical wording to the audited article, so treated as uncorroborated rather than independently verified.

Raw CBS figure (87.2k vs 52.3k expat entries in October) is exactly accurate (CBS release 345/2026). The headline's framing of this as a measure of 'how many came to vote' is a reasonable but imprecise reading: the body text makes no voting claim, CBS doesn't track visit purpose, and at most the above-baseline portion (~35k) is plausibly election-linked per independent reporting (Calcalist/Bekesher data, AIDC survey).

All 7 claims (OpenAI self-reported figures via Adam Fry's Big Technology interview, plus third-party Google/Bing market-share figures) matched their sources. Self-reported OpenAI metrics flagged as inherently unauditable beyond matching the quoted statement.

excluded_by_scope_count: non-exhaustive - 328 new candidate headlines were triaged by direct batch review (no separate cheap-model triage subagent used), not individually tagged per the spec's yes/maybe/no+excluded labeling
excluded_by_scope_examples: globes: "יותר מרבע מהח"כים הן נשים: שיא מאז קום המדינה" (official/factual tally of the just-completed election's results - headcount of a fixed, undisputed process)

themarker/haaretz: NICE/SolarEdge/Kamtech/Amdocs/Taboola quarterly earnings and single-day stock moves (company-reported earnings releases and trading moves - market-data analog, nothing to verify against a separate primary source)
ynet: "51 מורחקים במשחק אחד: הקטטה ההמונית בברזיל ששברה את שיא גינס" (single-match event measurement/record, not a disputed study)
ynet: "יום אחד, 9,200 חיילים בודדים" (headcount of a defined program population - official registry/factual tally)
Overwhelming majority of the 2-day window: Israeli election results/consultations, US midterm results, and day-to-day war/security/crime event coverage - not data stories by the spec's definition
notes: Unusually thin day for data stories: the 2-day window was dominated almost entirely by the Israeli election aftermath (presidential consultations, Shin Bet inquiry, coalition talks) and the US midterms - both fall under the registry/factual-tally and election-polls exclusions almost by construction. No cross-outlet clusters were found among the 5 audited stories (each sourced from a single outlet); none reached the red-flag verdicts (contradicted/unsupported/misinterpreted/cherry_picked) this cycle.
